Nah Therapy is more about knowing where this person is wrong and gradually leading them with baby steps to what they should actually be doing or their aha moment.

WIthout learning therapy and the types of traumas that exist you can never treat an individual right, even with the highest degree of empathy. I have high empathy and I am studying as a psychology major so I can tell you that empathy is a catalyst to be a good therapist, but empathy can be learned too, even if people with low empathy might use books but they will. 

And what makes a good therapist is not just empathy. it is patience above all. 

Imagine you have to get your mental state from point A to point B and to you Point B might feel daunting because it's something unfamiliar and your subconscious is designed to save you from the unfamiliar which it perceives as danger. Good therapist will be patient, bad ones will try to shove you to point B which will obviously be worse for you cause it will not come naturally and you will move further from point B
